visual.title: Grandma Rose's Blueberry Muffins
visual.note: Ask an adult to help you use the oven.
rows: Heat the oven to 375°F. Put paper cups in a 12-cup muffin pan.
In a large bowl, stir together 2 cups of flour, 1/2 cup of sugar and 2 teaspoons of baking powder.
In a small bowl, whisk 1 egg, 1 cup of milk and 1/3 cup of melted butter.
Pour the wet mix into the dry mix. Stir only until no dry flour shows. A few lumps are fine.
Gently fold in 1 cup of blueberries. If your berries are frozen, add them straight from the freezer.
Fill each paper cup about two-thirds full.
Bake for 20 minutes. Then poke a toothpick into the middle muffin.
If the toothpick comes out clean, the muffins are done. If it has wet batter on it, bake 4 more minutes and test again.
Let the muffins cool in the pan for 5 minutes before you lift them out.

passages.title: Planting Bean Seeds
sentences: Ms. Ortiz gave each pair in her class a sheet of directions for planting bean seeds in the school garden.
Before you plant, check how wet the soil is in your garden bed.
Push one finger into the soil, all the way down to your second knuckle.
If the soil feels dry at that depth, pour one full watering can over the bed and wait ten minutes.
If it already feels damp, you can begin planting right away.
Next, use the inch marks on your trowel handle to make a straight row of holes.
Each hole should be about one inch deep, and the holes should be four inches apart.
Drop one bean seed into each hole, and then gently cover it with loose soil.
Do not press the soil down hard, because the young roots need air to grow.
Finally, push a craft-stick label into the end of your row.
Write both of your names and today's date on the label in pencil, since marker ink can wash off in the rain.
Water the row lightly, just until the top of the soil looks dark.
The first green shoots should appear in about seven to ten days.

passages.title: Calibrating the Rover's Distance Sensor
sentences: Priya's rover uses a distance sensor to stop before it bumps into a wall.
The sensor sends out a sound too high for people to hear, and then it measures how long the echo takes to bounce back.
Before each competition, the robotics club calibrates the sensor, which means checking that its readings match real, measured distances.
To begin, place the rover on a flat table with its sensor facing a cardboard box.
Use a ruler to measure exactly 20 centimeters from the front of the sensor to the box.
Next, connect the rover to the club laptop with the USB cable and open the program called SensorCheck.
Press the Read button three times, and write down each number that appears on the screen.
Now compare your three readings with the real distance of 20 centimeters.
If all three readings are between 19 and 21 centimeters, the sensor is accurate, and you can unplug the cable.
If the readings are all too high or all too low, type the difference into the Offset box and press Save.
For example, if the sensor reads 23 centimeters each time, the difference is 3, so you type minus 3.
Then press Read three more times to make sure your fix worked.
Sometimes the three numbers jump around instead, such as 15, 28 and 20.
Jumping numbers usually mean that the sensor is dusty or that the box is too small to send back a clear echo.
In that case, wipe the sensor gently with a dry cloth, move to a larger box, and start the whole test again from the beginning.

passages.title: Setting Up a Weather Station
sentences: Priya's family bought a SkyCheck weather station for their backyard.
It has two parts: an outdoor sensor and an indoor display.
The sensor measures the temperature and the humidity outside, and it sends the numbers to the display by radio.
Humidity means how much water vapor is in the air.
First, put two AA batteries into the outdoor sensor.
Within one minute, put three AAA batteries into the display, so the display can connect to the sensor.
Keep both parts on the same table while they connect.
After about three minutes, the outdoor temperature should appear on the screen.
If you still see two dashes instead of a number, take the batteries out of the display, wait ten seconds, and put them back in.
Next, choose a home for the sensor.
Hang it on a post about five feet above the ground, in a spot that is shady all day, such as under a tree.
Sunlight shining on the sensor makes it read warmer than the air really is.
Keep it away from walls, roofs and driveways too, because they soak up the sun's heat and give it off later.
Last, set the display indoors, no more than 100 feet from the sensor.

visual.title: TumbleMax Rock Tumbler: Polishing Guide
rows: 1. Shape
2 spoons of coarse grit
7 days
Rocks have no sharp edges. If some still do, repeat Stage 1 for 7 more days.
2. Smooth
2 spoons of medium grit
7 days
Rocks feel smooth all over.
3. Fine
2 spoons of fine grit
7 days
Rocks look dull but feel very smooth.
4. Polish
2 spoons of polish powder
7 days
Rocks shine when they are dry. If they look cloudy, repeat Stage 4.
visual.note: Every stage: fill the barrel two-thirds full of rocks, add the grit, then add water until it almost covers the rocks. Between stages, wash the rocks and the barrel well, because even a few grains of old grit can scratch the rocks. Put the old mud in the trash, not the sink, because it can block the pipes. Ask an adult to help you check the tumbler each day.

passages.title: Tide Pool Checklist
sentences: Ms. Ortiz is taking the science club to the tide pools at Harbor Point on Saturday.
A tide pool is a shallow pocket of seawater that remains trapped among the rocks after the tide goes out.
Sea stars, hermit crabs, periwinkle snails and sea anemones all live in these pools.
Before the trip, Ms. Ortiz sent every club member this checklist.
First, check the tide table, because you can reach the pools only when the tide is low.
On Saturday, low tide at Harbor Point is at 10:40 AM.
Plan to reach the rocks about one hour before low tide.
Start walking back to the sand no later than one hour after low tide, because the water keeps rising and covers the low rocks.
If you lose track of the time, listen for Ms. Ortiz, who will blow her whistle three times when it is time to go back.
Next, pack your bag the night before.
Wear old sneakers or water shoes with sturdy rubber soles, because wet seaweed makes the rocks extremely slippery.
Bring a hat, a water bottle, and a notebook and pencil for your field notes.
Leave buckets and nets at home, because every creature must remain in its own pool.
At the pools, observe carefully before you touch anything.
If you want to touch an animal, wet your hand in the pool first and use only one finger, very gently.
Never pull an animal off a rock, because many of them attach themselves firmly to the rock, and pulling can injure them.
If you lift a small rock to look underneath, put it back exactly the way it was, because animals live on its underside.

passages.title: Tuning a Guitar
sentences: Sam is learning to play the guitar in the Harbor Middle School music club.
Before every practice, he tunes his guitar, which means making each string play exactly the right note.
A guitar has six strings, and in standard tuning they are E, A, D, G, B and E, from the thickest string to the thinnest.
The club leader gave Sam these steps for using a clip-on tuner.
First, clip the tuner onto the head of the guitar, where the tuning pegs are, and switch it on.
Next, pluck the thickest string once and let it ring.
The tuner shows the letter of the note it hears, along with a needle.
If the needle points left of the center, the note is flat, or too low, so slowly turn that string's peg to tighten the string.
If the needle points right of the center, the note is sharp, or too high, so loosen the string a little.
When the needle stays in the center and the screen turns green, that string is in tune.
Strings stay in tune longer when you finish by tightening, so if you go past the note, loosen the string below it and then tighten it back up.
Repeat these steps for each of the other five strings, from thickest to thinnest.
Sometimes the tuner shows the wrong letter, such as G when you are tuning the A string.
In music, G is the note just below A, so that string is much too low, and you should keep tightening it slowly until the letter changes to A.
Always turn the pegs slowly, because a string that is pulled much too tight can snap.
When all six strings are in tune, check each one again, because tuning one string pulls a little on the others.

items.hint: Find the step about ribs. Read it to the very end.
items.explain: The biggest rib goes on first. Step 3 says to slide the ribs on from the biggest rib to the smallest.

items.prompt: Sam finds a small piece with the number 14 on it. He does not know where it goes. What should he do?
options: Find number 14 on the picture card
Put it on the display base
Leave it out of the model
Push it into the skull
items.hint: Find the step that talks about the numbers on the pieces.
items.explain: He finds number 14 on the picture card. Step 1 says each piece has a number that matches the picture card.

items.prompt: Ben's dad is on a phone call in the next room. Ben wants to practice without sound coming from the speakers. What should he do before he presses POWER?
options: Plug his headphones into the PHONES hole
Turn the VOLUME knob to the middle
Press VOICE and choose 01 Piano
Fold up the stand
items.hint: Look for a step about playing quietly. Check that it comes before the POWER step.
items.explain: He plugs his headphones into the PHONES hole. Step 3 says to do this to play quietly, and it comes before pressing POWER.

items.prompt: The keyboard is plugged in. Tap the buttons and the knob Ben uses, in order.
items.hint: Read the last three steps on the card. Tap each thing as its step names it.
items.explain: Ben presses POWER, turns the VOLUME knob, then presses VOICE. Steps 4, 5 and 6 name them in that order. The card does not use the TEMPO button.

items.prompt: Priya put batteries in both parts. Three minutes later, the display still shows two dashes. What should she do?
options: Move the sensor into the sun so it warms up
Take the display batteries out, wait ten seconds, and put them back in
Take the sensor batteries out and buy new ones
Hang the sensor on the post, then check the display again
items.hint: Find the sentence that starts with If. Check that what it describes matches what Priya sees.
items.explain: She takes the display batteries out, waits ten seconds, and puts them back in. The second paragraph says to do this if you still see two dashes.

items.prompt: Where should Priya hang the sensor?
options: Five feet up on a post in the sunny middle of the yard
Five feet up on a post under a shady tree
Five feet up on the shady side of the house wall
On the ground under a shady tree
items.hint: The third paragraph gives three rules for the sensor's spot. Check each choice against all three rules.
items.explain: She hangs it five feet up on a post under a shady tree. The third paragraph says to hang it about five feet up, in a spot that is shady all day, and away from walls.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that tells why the sensor must be in the shade.
items.hint: Look for a sentence that gives a reason, not an instruction.
items.explain: The sentence is "Sunlight shining on the sensor makes it read warmer than the air really is." It is in the third paragraph.

items.prompt: Maya opens the barrel after Stage 1. Most rocks are round now, but two still have sharp edges. What should she do?
options: Go on to Stage 2, because the 7 days are done
Repeat Stage 1 for 7 more days
Wash the rocks and add the polish powder
Add 2 spoons of medium grit to the same muddy water
items.hint: Find the Check column for Stage 1. Read what to do if the check fails.
items.explain: She repeats Stage 1 for 7 more days. The Stage 1 row says that if some rocks still have sharp edges, repeat Stage 1.

items.prompt: Stage 1 is done. Maya is starting Stage 2. Put her steps in order.
steps: Wash the rocks and the barrel well
Fill the barrel two-thirds full of rocks
Add 2 spoons of medium grit
Add water until it almost covers the rocks
Run the tumbler for 7 days
items.hint: The note under the table tells you what to do between stages and at the start of every stage. Use it with the Stage 2 row.
items.explain: She washes everything, fills the barrel with rocks, adds the medium grit, adds water, then runs it for 7 days. The note gives the order, and the Stage 2 row gives the grit and the time.

items.prompt: Maya has to repeat Stage 1 once. The other stages work the first time. How many days of tumbling will it take in all?
options: 28 days
35 days
42 days
14 days
items.hint: Count how many times Maya runs a stage, including the repeat. Then multiply by the days in each stage.
items.explain: It takes 35 days. She runs five stages of 7 days each: Stage 1 twice, then Stages 2, 3 and 4.

items.prompt: Leo walks south from the bridge and comes to the campsite, not the mill. What should he do?
options: Stamp his card at the campsite
Go back to the bridge and count his steps again
Follow the yellow trail markers back to the start
Keep walking south until he finds the mill
items.hint: Find the step that names the campsite. Read what it tells you to do.
items.explain: He goes back to the bridge and counts his steps again. Step 5 says that reaching the campsite means you have gone too far.

items.prompt: Leo has just stamped box 2 at the bridge. What should he do next?
options: Walk north 200 steps
Cross the bridge, then walk south 150 steps
Walk east along the creek to the bridge
Follow the yellow trail markers to the start
items.hint: Find the step with Checkpoint 2. Then read the step right after it.
items.explain: He crosses the bridge and walks south 150 steps. Step 4 comes right after Checkpoint 2 at the bridge.

items.prompt: When should Sam plan to reach the rocks, and what is the latest time he should start walking back?
options: Reach them at 9:40 AM, and start back by 11:40 AM
Reach them at 10:40 AM, and start back by 11:40 AM
Reach them at 9:40 AM, and start back by 10:40 AM
Reach them at 9:40 AM, and start back by 12:40 PM
items.hint: Find the low tide time first. Then use the two sentences after it to count one hour back and one hour forward.
items.explain: He should reach the rocks at about 9:40 AM and start back by 11:40 AM. Low tide is at 10:40 AM, and the checklist says to arrive one hour before and start back no later than one hour after.

items.prompt: Maya lifts a small rock and finds snails stuck to the bottom. She has finished looking. What should she do?
options: Put the rock back exactly the way it was
Put the rock back upside down so the snails get some sun
Gently pull the snails off and drop them in the pool
Carry the rock to the sand so others can see it
items.hint: Find the sentence about lifting a rock. Then check each choice against the sentence before it too.
items.explain: She puts the rock back exactly the way it was. The last sentence says animals live on a rock's underside, and the sentence before it says never to pull an animal off a rock.

items.prompt: When does each step happen? Put each step in the right box.
bins: When it is time to go

cards.text: Pack a hat and a water bottle
Wet your hand before you touch an animal
Walk back when the whistle blows three times
Pack a notebook and a pencil
Put a lifted rock back the way it was
Start back to the sand by 11:40 AM

items.hint: Find each step in the checklist. Read which paragraph it is in and what that paragraph is about.
items.explain: Packing the hat, water, notebook and pencil happens the night before. Wetting your hand and putting rocks back happen at the pools. Walking back by 11:40 AM or at three whistle blasts happens when it is time to go.

items.prompt: Sam plucks the D string. The tuner shows D, but the needle points to the right of the center. What should he do?
options: Tighten the string, because the note is too low
Loosen the string a little below the note, then tighten it back up to D
Leave it, because the tuner already shows D
Keep tightening the string until the tuner shows E
items.hint: Decide if the note is flat or sharp. Then read the sentence about finishing by tightening.
items.explain: He loosens the string a little, then tightens it back up to D. The needle on the right means the note is sharp, or too high, and the text says to finish by tightening up to the note.

items.prompt: Sam is tuning the B string, but the tuner shows A. What should he do?
options: Loosen the string slowly until the tuner shows B
Tighten the string slowly until the tuner shows B
Tune the A string instead, because the tuner shows A
Unclip the tuner and pluck the thinnest string
items.hint: Find the example about the wrong letter. Think about which letter comes just before B, and use the example the same way.
items.explain: He tightens the string slowly until the tuner shows B. In the example, G is just below A, so the string is too low. A is just below B, so this string is too low too.

items.prompt: Put Sam's tuning steps in order.
steps: Clip on the tuner and switch it on
Pluck the thickest string
Turn its peg until the needle stays in the center
Tune the other five strings the same way
Check all six strings again
items.hint: Use the order words First and Next. Remember that the final check happens after every string is done.
items.explain: Clip on the tuner, pluck the thickest string, tune it until the needle stays centered, tune the other five strings, then check all six again. The last sentence says to check each string again when all six are in tune.

steps.say: I need to put the steps in order. I look for order words like first, then and last.
This step starts with First. The banana and berries go in first.
This step starts with Then. The milk goes in next.
This step starts with Last. The lid goes on and they press START at the end.
So the order is fruit, then milk, then the lid and START.
